articles.title: Hideo Kojima Makes Surprise Cameo in New My Chemical Romance Animated Short
articles.summary: Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima showed up for a cameo role in a new animated short from legendary rock outfit My Chemical Romance. That's probably not the first sentence you expected to read heading into the Halloween weekend, but considering Kojima is known for his love of music, movies…
body: The seven-and-a-half-minute project, which arrived as a surprise drop yesterday evening, is a stop-motion, dark fairytale based on director Lauren Tsai's The Dying World. Serving as a vehicle for a 20th anniversary music video for My Chemical Romance's "The End." – the opening track for the New Jersey group's seminal rock record, The Black Parade – the video also enlisted Kojima for a quick voice role.

Just as main character, Astrid, retreats to her room to parse through a few missed calls, we get Kojima's My Chemical Romance music video debut. He's credited simply as The Teacher, and can be heard scolding Astrid about late work in her third voicemail. You can see the full text below.
"Astrid your Japanese homework is late again. This is unacceptab-" Kojima's The Teacher can be heard saying before the recording is cut off.

articles.title: Everything Coming to Prime Video in November
articles.summary: November is one of the most important times of the year for Amazon, thanks to Black Friday sales. So it's not surprising that Amazon's Prime Video would have an absolutely stacked slate of upcoming releases to entice new subscribers this month.
body: Along with the usual dump of movies getting added to the platform on November 1, we'll get quite a few highly anticipated Prime Video Originals. There's a Muhammand Ali series, Season 3 of Rings of Power, the Madden Movie, and a new Blade Runner series all premiering this month.

If you're wondering how to make the most of your Prime Video subscription this month, I've curated a quick selection of movies and shows that are absolutely worth your time. You can also jump to the full list of November releases to see the full breakdown by day.

Amazon, like every other streaming service, is dropping a bunch of Christmas movies onto its streaming service starting on November 1. Among this year's selection, there's one somewhat hidden gem worth highlighting: Jingle All the Way.

This is an Arnold Schwarzenegger film where he plays a mattress salesman who promises to get his son the year's hottest toy for Christmas, only to find out it's sold out everywhere. It's a ridiculous movie centered around consumerism that everyone needs to watch at least once.

articles.title: The 10 Best Star Trek: The Next Generation Episodes, Ranked
articles.summary: One of the great things about Star Trek: The Next Generation is that you never quite knew what kind of adventure you were going to get. One week, the Enterprise might be facing an enemy capable of destroying the Federation.
body: That variety was part of the show's appeal. Over seven seasons, The Next Generation could deliver thrilling science-fiction adventures, tackle complicated moral questions, and occasionally make viewers laugh out loud. But what made the series special wasn't just the stories. It was the characters and the relationships that developed among them, giving even the most far-fetched adventures a human connection.

Nearly 40 years after its premiere, the best episodes remain just as enjoyable to revisit. Some are remembered for their ambitious ideas, others for a particular performance, a heartbreaking moment or a perfectly delivered line. Not every episode on this list is flawless, but each has something that makes it unforgettable. And that's a pretty good measure of great Star Trek.

Few Star Trek episodes grab your attention like "Cause and Effect," which opens with the Enterprise exploding. The crew is trapped in a temporal loop that repeatedly ends in the ship's destruction, with each cycle offering clues that something isn't right.
points: One of the great things about Star Trek: The Next Generation is that you never quite knew what kind of adventure you were going to get.
One week, the Enterprise might be facing an enemy capable of destroying the Federation.
Over seven seasons, The Next Generation could deliver thrilling science-fiction adventures, tackle complicated moral questions, and occasionally make viewers laugh out loud.
Nearly 40 years after its premiere, the best episodes remain just as enjoyable to revisit.

articles.title: Bungie Says 'Don't Buy Marathon as a Donation' as Destiny Players Look to Support Studio's Future
articles.summary: As Bungie plots a future for more Destiny, head of product Josh Deane has clarified that players don't need to "buy Marathon as a donation" just to support the studio's plans.
body: It's a clarification that arrived after Deane posted a community message for Destiny fans yesterday. The message, featured as part of a lengthy Q&A blog post, outlined the unvaulting process for Destiny 2 content that was previously promised last month, but one segment left players confused – and concerned – about the future and extraction shooter Marathon's role in the big picture.

"We're not going to forget the mistakes of the past, but it's time to learn from them and unify as one Bungie community," the section in question said. "For us, the majority of our Bungie team is legacy Destiny, and we will all tell you that nothing can help bridge us into future more than for Marathon to rapidly evolve and become sustainable. As we head into our December and March updates for Marathon, it’s a formative period for all of us here at Bungie that will help determine the shape of our future, so please encourage each other and know that your support gives our team the energy to finish the fight."

articles.title: New Pokémon Release Brings Hundreds of New Eeveelutions
articles.summary: With eight official Eeveelutions, fans of the beloved normal-type Pokémon aren't hurting for options — yet paradoxically, they're also one of the most neglected segments of the fandom. After all, it's been 13 years since Game Freak introduced a new Eevee monster in Pokémon X and Pokémon Y.
body: Pokémon Winds and Waves could potentially introduce a new Eevee, but that game doesn't seem to be coming out any time soon. Rather than get their hopes up for something that is extremely unlikely, though, Eevee devotees might be better served by playing a new fan game called Pokémon Oops! All Eevees.

Despite the name, the fan game isn't a one-trick Ponyta. Yes, every monster in the game has been replaced with an Eeveelution, but creator 999999999 has also introduced all sorts of original Eevee designs into the experience as well. There's a ghost-type Eevee called Fanteon, a flying-type creature called Aeraerieon, and a fighting-type Eeveelution called Aercampeon, just to name a few. The fan game isn't afraid to double-dip into existing Eeveelution types, either. Many of these new designs have their own evolution lines.

All told, Oops! All Eevees introduces an astonishing 326 Eeveelutions into the base Pokémon FireRed game. A video that quickly speeds through all the available monsters in this fan game runs nearly 40 minutes.
points: With eight official Eeveelutions, fans of the beloved normal-type Pokémon aren't hurting for options — yet paradoxically, they're also one of the most neglected segments of the fandom.
After all, it's been 13 years since Game Freak introduced a new Eevee monster in Pokémon X and Pokémon Y.

articles.title: EA Just Shelved A Mysterious Sims Project—That Could Be Good News For Players
articles.summary: It's been another rough year for video games, with countless studio closures, staff layoffs, and projects that barely managed to even get off the ground before they were unceremoniously cut short.
body: This was especially painful for Mass Effect players, who were looking forward to the upcoming Mass Effect 5, which we now know was tentatively titled Mass Effect: Universe. But it's not just BioWare fans who are upset at the moment. Fans of EA's other properties are growing increasingly concerned about the future of those franchises, if any future is planned for them at all. My colleague Levi Winslow recently wrote about their concerns for the Skate franchise in the wake of layoffs at its development studio. Meanwhile, I'm quite worried about the fate of The Sims.

In the same breath it announced the end of BioWare, EA also reaffirmed its commitment to Apex Legends, Skate, and The Sims franchises. But everyone knows that when it comes to profits, EA's sports titles outrun its other IPs by a country mile. If EA is willing to pull the plug on legacy franchises like Mass Effect and Dragon Age, where does that leave its other franchises, like The Sims 4?

articles.title: CoD: Modern Warfare To Cut Real-Life Korean Tragedy Segment After Backlash
articles.summary: Publisher Activision has responded to criticism over using a devastating tragedy in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, saying that the incident will be removed from the military shooter in a November 12 update. The Seoul Halloween crowd crush occurred in October 2022 in Itaewon.
body: "Using such an incident as material for a game intended for entertainment purposes is itself highly inappropriate and a senseless act," the groups said, according to the BBC. "The Itaewon tragedy was a tragic disaster that produced hundreds of casualties, and citizens who participated in the rescue efforts or witnessed the event at the time continue to suffer from trauma. If the game developer has even a minimum level of courtesy and empathy toward the victims, they should promptly take corrective measures."

Activision has heard the call and plans to remove the depiction from Modern Warfare 4 when an update arrives on November 12. In responding to the criticism, Activision said it never intended to trivialize the disaster or make light of human suffering.

"In developing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, we approached the subject matter with care and respect. The game’s opening cinematic utilises some real-world news coverage to establish the game’s fictional narrative," Activision said. "It is not intended to reference or trivialise the Itaewon disaster or any other real-world tragedy in any way, shape or form."

articles.title: The Witcher 3’s Fairy Tale-Inspired Quests Are Must-Plays for Any RPG Fan
articles.summary: As a franchise spanning video games, books, and a television series, The Witcher owes everything to 300-year-old fairy tales. The very first book, The Last Wish (which itself is a collection of short stories set in The Witcher universe), has a number of fairy tale references, including "A Grain of…
body: These inspirations continue through The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, widely considered to be one of the best RPGs of all time. The third game in the series by CD Projekt Red famously raised the bar for the quality of its side quests, and there are two that truly embody that fairy tale formula, albeit with much darker themes.

First up, and by far the most memorable of the pair as it's from the base game, is "Ladies of the Wood." If you've played The Witcher 3, you'll recall the Crones of Crookback Bog; a trio of witches who live in the swamp, known as the Weavess, Brewess, and Whispess. They are, for all intents and purposes, grotesque as hell. The three are sisters and daughters of the original Lady of the Wood, whose spirit lives beneath an ancient oak tree nearby, after the Crones killed her.

articles.title: New Assassin’s Creed Game Is Out Now, If You Don’t Mind Being Board
articles.summary: If you thought there wasn't going to be a new Assassin's Creed game this year, think again. It's not a video game, but Assassin's Creed: Animus is out today, turning the series into an adventure-style board game for 1-4 players.
body: A competitive game that pits players against each other as they explore distinct eras from the video games, Assassin's Creed: Animus features four protagonists to choose from in its standard edition: Eivor, Ezio, Altair, and Connor. The Collector's Edition, meanwhile, expands to 10 eras and features 16 protagonists, adding game characters like Edward Kenway, Jacob and Evie Frye, and Kassandra.

You and up to three of your friends (or you alone) work to complete objectives across these eras, taking down assassination targets in the way you see fit via "memory blocks." Whether you go in with your sword drawn or engage in a sneakier approach is up to you.

The standard version of Assassin's Creed: Animus is available to order now for $65, while the limited Collector's Edition costs $229. Alongside the extra characters and eras, this version comes with a storage box, acrylic tokens, a metal Piece of Eden, a cloth token bag, "special event cards," and an Animus Card Holder.

articles.title: The Worst GTA Game Is One Rockstar Could Never Make Today
articles.summary: GTA Advance is an odd game. It's terrible in some ways, yet also not as bad as its reputation suggests. It's also an essential part of Rockstar history. This was Rockstar at a stage of uncertainty.
body: Mike's struggles take a backseat to your struggle of getting through GTA Advance, though. Digital Eclipse and Rockstar's ambition outstripped the Game Boy Advance's capabilities, and the poor little system struggles to keep up with the game. Framerates are awful, and the controls are terribly clunky. Well, most Rockstar games have clunky controls, but when everything you need to do is confined to fewer buttons laid out across a smaller space, things get more complicated than they need to be.

Which is a shame, as GTA Advance is a fascinating look at GTA's adolescence, one worth examining even if it does suck to play. It's Rockstar in an uncharacteristically indecisive moment, trying to fuse modern GTA with the series' classic top-down style, marketed to an audience that probably didn't plan on buying a GTA game when they picked up the tiny purple handheld. GTA Advance tries adapting the open-ended nature of its 3D siblings to the hardware constraints of the Game Boy Advance, and Rockstar even marketed it as a continuation of the 3D games.
points: It's terrible in some ways, yet also not as bad as its reputation suggests.
It's also an essential part of Rockstar history.

articles.title: GOTY hopeful Mina the Hollower bought the studio financial stability "for now," while the Shovel Knight devs work on a new 3D game
articles.summary: Yacht Club Games has confirmed that most of its developers are now working on a brand new 3D game (potentially Shovel Knight 3D), after the critically-acclaimed Mina the Hollower did well enough for the team to continue.
body: Before launching its old-school adventure game earlier this year, Yacht Club described Mina the Hollower as a "make-or-break" moment for the beloved indie studio. A global pandemic and a failed experiment to turn Yacht Club into a multi-project studio had left the developer on thin ice, it seems.

But Mina the Hollower sold well enough to buy the studio more time, according to a new Reddit AMA full of interesting tidbits. Asked if Mina was able to secure financial stability for the company, Sean Velasco simply said "yes… for now!" Mina managed to sell over 500,000 copies in its first two weeks, so it's well on its way to the one million copies the devs were once hoping for.

For the foreseeable future, the devs aren't ready to talk about the kinds of DLC and spin-offs and follow-ups that dear old Shovel Knight enjoyed for many years, but they're not abandoning their newest baby either. "We're working on more post-release features," the devs wrote, which includes "expanded randomizer options, enemy and boss randomization, more modifiers, speedrunner features" and more ways "to do even more in Mina."

articles.title: Blizzard hints at console ports for World of Warcraft: Forever - "Play it wherever you want and, at some point, on whatever you want"
articles.summary: After more than two decades dominating the PC MMO battlefield, it sounds like Blizzard Entertainment 's taking the idea of a World of Warcraft console port more seriously than ever.
body: World of Warcraft: Forever's beta seems to have been immensely popular with fans of the series. It's a brand new third version of the iconic multiplayer game that sits alongside WoW's Classic and Retail portions, and it's recaptured many a lapsed Warcraft sicko with tons of good changes, big and small - one of which is controller support for the first time ever.

Speaking to GamesRadar about the decision to keep World of Warcraft: Forever exclusive to PC players, despite now supporting gamepads, vice president and executive producer Holly Longdale hinted that the fantasy game might just make its way to even more devices and players over time.

"What you just described is really what we're after," she told the outlet. "Play it wherever you want and, at some point, on whatever you want. But the first leg of that journey is getting gamepads working really well with World of Warcraft, and we thought Forever was the perfect place to start."

articles.title: Soulframe opens up for everyone next week as the Warframe devs prepare the fantasy action RPG for one of its 'biggest, most violent' updates ever next month
articles.summary: After three years of invite-only playtests, Soulframe is opening its doors to everyone next week on November 6. If you've been waiting to see what the developers of Warframe are doing with a fantasy action RPG, you'll finally be able to jump in and see for yourself.
body: The transition to an open alpha will be followed by a massive transformation to the structure of the game later in November. Midrath, Soulframe's big open landmass, won't be the verdant, almost chill, place it used to be: The entire area will be corrupted and it's your job to bring it back to life. "You're going to enter a game that is much more unforgiving and harsh at first glance," creative director Geoff Crookes explained in a recent presentation attended by PC Gamer.

This update, Prelude 17 or Verse of the Veillands, is a huge shift for Soulframe, but an important one that will help new players acclimate to the world. Crookes said the goal is to improve the onboarding experience and to give players "much more ownership" over their decisions early on. It won't be fully finished yet, however, so what's in there today is just "the functional bones" of what will come in the final game.
points: After three years of invite-only playtests, Soulframe is opening its doors to everyone next week on November 6.

videos.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 - Official 'From Launch to Live': From the Ward Ep. 8
videos.summary: Watch the final 'From the Ward' episode for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 for a behind-the-scenes look at the making of the first-person shooter game and the process of creating live seasons.
body: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is available now on PlayStation 5 (PS5), Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC (Steam).
points: Watch the final 'From the Ward' episode for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 for a behind-the-scenes look at the making of the first-person shooter game and the process of creating live seasons.
Join the development team at Infinity Ward as they discuss what's ahead with live seasons, and how stories, characters, Multiplayer, DMZ, and Call of Duty: Warzone come together in the journey ahead.
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is available now on PlayStation 5 (PS5), Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC (Steam).
